name: K-Board
summary: Single-port family whose application and bootloader both report as K-Board; bootloader state is distinguished by PID MSB = 1.

notes: The device's SysEx preamble parser (shared between K-Board's firmware and bootloader) stops reading as soon as the fixed 6-byte preamble is decoded, without regard for the 7-bit/8-bit decode's group boundaries. Without a flush after the preamble, the first payload byte of a following command can land in the same decode group as the preamble's tail and get silently dropped.
Without requiresFlushAfterPreamble, an affected command is silently no-op'd rather than rejected, which can look like a successful send that simply did nothing.

The bootloader unconditionally erases the whole application region on the first valid firmware packet, blocking further USB service until that finishes - same behavior as KBP4, though K-Board tolerates a larger first window (64B vs KBP4's 32B) before an in-flight send itself starts failing mid-transmission.

K-Board reboots straight into application mode as it commits the final chunk and never answers an identity request in bootloader mode afterwards; the application-port reconnect and version check is the real success test.
Requests a reboot into bootloader mode while the device still reports as K-Board.
Preferred current production K-Board firmware payload. Chunk-safe (-cs512) packaging.
Adds finalizeTareCapture(): a one-time +25% margin applied to the settled boot-time tare average for key/button/bend-pad sensors, capped at 2/3 of range, to reduce reported key over-sensitivity.

NOT a production release. Performance-test firmware variant (perf_test branch of k-board-firmware) that emits synthetic MIDI/SysEx traffic on command and disables physical key/bend-pad input, used to stress-test mimic_hub with up to 13 simultaneous K-Boards.
Version 9.0.1 is deliberately out of the normal release sequence so it's unmistakable in an ID reply. Select explicitly with --fw-version 9.0.1; never the implicit default.
See k-board-firmware's .buddy-project/kboard-perf-test-design.md for the full design and SYX_CMD_TEST_MODE/SYX_CMD_BURST_MODE command reference.
Bootloader uses the same reported product string as the application; confirm state via PID MSB = 1.
